title: Session-aware active-active failover with circuit-breaker and load-shed policy for hosted gateway
creator: Avery Chen
description: Summary: Implement session-aware active-active failover behavior in the hosted API gateway to preserve streaming sessions and request affinity while meeting SLOs during multi-region incidents. Background: We currently perform region failover at a coarse level which leads to dropped streaming sessions and unexpected session-affinity breaks for customers using long-lived websocket/SSE connections or multi-request sessions with KV cache dependency. This ticket scopes design, implementation, and rollout of traffic-shifting policies that are aware of session state, incorporate circuit-breaker thresholds, and perform graceful load shedding for non-critical requests.
goals: 1) Preserve in-flight streaming sessions for at least 60s during partial regional degradations where possible. 2) Ensure 99.9% successful request completion for non-streaming requests when both regions are healthy; degrade non-critical pathways first under overload. 3) Define and enforce circuit-breaker thresholds integrated with per-route SLOs and automatic routing fallback. 4) Provide telemetry and runbook hooks for on-call to observe session retention, failover rate, and load-shed events.
non_goals: 1) Full state replication between regions for custom customer session stores. 2) Re-architecting session APIs for customers. 3) Large-scale KV cache replication beyond short-lived prefix caching and header-level hints.
constraints: - Must work with existing smart-router and edge-inference proxies. - Minimal latency impact for steady-state; target p95 increase <10ms for session-aware routing. - No schema changes to public API. - Rollout must allow rollback within 30 minutes.
high_level_approach: 1) Introduce session token propagation (opaque header) that indicates session affinity, session age, and KV cache hints. 2) Router policy: for requests with active session token, prefer origin region; if origin region signals degraded (circuit open), attempt graceful rejoin by streaming sink forwarding or session handoff when possible. 3) Streaming preservation: for server-streaming and websockets, implement streaming proxy buffers at edge that attempt reconnect/replay for up to 60s and coordinate with circuit-breaker states to decide whether to wait or redirect. 4) Load-shedding tiers: critical (inference completion), best-effort (priority <X), telemetry-only. 5) Metrics/telemetry: per-session failover rate, session-drop-by-cause, circuit-breaker-trigger-count, shed-request-count, latency shift by cohort.
technical_tradeoffs: - Option A: Active session handoff with state transfer introduces complexity and small window for duplication; better UX for customers but higher implementation risk. - Option B: Prefer origin for a tie-breaker and let clients reconnect; simpler but results in dropped connections for some customers. We propose starting with Option B plus edge buffering and a later opt-in handoff mechanism. - Preferring header-based session tokens avoids database lookups but requires client cooperation and may leak heuristics.
rollout_plan: Phase 1: Canary (5% of traffic) with non-production customers and internal test tokens. Phase 2: 25% traffic with session-preserving buffer enabled. Phase 3: 100% traffic with load-shed tiers active and circuit-breaker integrated. Each phase 48h observation window and automatic rollback if session-drop rate increases >5% above baseline.
acceptance_criteria: - Streaming session drop rate does not increase by more than 3% in canary. - Circuit-breaker opens/rejects traffic at configured thresholds with documented metrics. - p95 latency increase <10ms for normal traffic during canary. - Load-shedding evicts best-effort requests before critical ones, verified by test harness. - Runbook steps succeed in a simulated multi-region outage drill.
implementation_tasks: 1) Router: add session token-aware routing decision and fallbacks. 2) Edge proxy: implement 60s streaming buffer and reconnect hints. 3) Circuit-breaker: per-route thresholds hooked into router. 4) Load-shedding: implement priority queue and evictor. 5) Telemetry: new metrics and dashboard. 6) E2E tests and chaos injection scenarios.
testing_notes: - unit tests for router decision matrix. - integration tests for handshake + streaming preserve across artificial region flaps. - chaos: kill region A for 30s during high QPS and assert graceful degradation. - synthetic load: validate shedding order and latency targets.
performance_targets: p50/p95/p99 latency targets unchanged for steady state; failover window <300ms for non-streaming requests when circuit is closed, <60s best-effort preservation for streaming sessions via buffering/reconnect hints.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create alerts: 'session_drop_rate > 1% over 5m', 'circuit_breaker_open_rate > 0.5% over 1m', 'shed_request_rate spike', 'failover_routings_without_session_token'. Dashboard: Gateway SLOs, per-region health, session retention cohorts.
safety_and_rollback: Feature flag gated rollout. Kill-switch at router level to disable session-aware behavior. Automatic rollback if acceptance criteria breached. Postmortem template for incidents linked in runbook.
open_questions: 1) How do we represent session affinity for third-party SDKs that cannot be changed? 2) Should handoff be synchronous or asynchronous? 3) Are there regulatory concerns for buffering sensitive payloads at edge?
decisions_made: 1) Initial implementation will not perform full session state replication; rely on edge buffering and client reconnects. 2) Circuit-breaker thresholds will be configurable per-route and default to 95th-percentile CPU or latency signals. 3) Session token header format will be opaque but base64-encoded to avoid header parsing issues.
review_feedback: PM (Maya Patel): emphasize customer opt-in for handoff. Security (Liam O'Neal): encrypt buffered payloads at rest and TTL 60s. Design (Raya Singh): expose developer-facing headers to indicate failover reason for better client UX.
timeline: Design: Feb 12 - Feb 26. Implementation: Feb 27 - Mar 22. Canary/Validation: Mar 23 - Apr 02.
notes: We will coordinate with Dedicated team to ensure routing policies are reusable for private deployments. Keep careful notes on KPI regressions during canary and collect sample request IDs for debugging. Use tracing hooks added in ENG-33122.
changelog: 2026-02-12: Ticket created by Avery Chen. 2026-02-25: Design reviewed and approved by stakeholders. 2026-03-01: Prototype of edge buffer merged (PR #211). 2026-03-08: Circuit-breaker integration tests added. 2026-03-12: Moved to In Progress and scheduled canary.
customer_notes: Beta customers will be contacted prior to canary. Provide docs explaining session token header and guidance for client reconnect logic.
implementation_risks: - Edge buffering may increase memory pressure on proxies under extreme load. - Mis-tuned circuit-breakers could cause cascading failovers. - Non-cooperative clients will see higher session drops.
mitigations: - Backpressure and per-connection memory caps. - Conservative default thresholds and staged ramp. - Telemetry to detect non-cooperative clients and automated rollback policy.
how_to_validate_post_release: Run region-flap exercise, validate session retention, confirm metrics against baseline, and run load-shed correctness tests. Solicit feedback from pilot customers.
implementation_notes: Prefer feature-flag gating and config driven thresholds. Keep logic stateless where possible and lean on centralized config via runtime-pack. Use existing tracing span names 'gateway.failover' and 'gateway.session-shift'.
